shower.thought: The only time you ever see your own face is when you're looking at a reflection or a photo—never the actual thing everyone else sees.
We treat our phones like they're extensions of ourselves, but we'd never let another person follow us around, recording everything we do.
Boredom might be your brain telling you it's not learning anything, which means bored people are actually the most aware of their own stagnation.
You've never actually tasted food the way someone else has—your brain is always flavoring it with your own memories and expectations.
The worst part about growing old isn't the physical decay; it's realizing how many people you'll never see again without knowing it was the last time.
Every time you remember something, you're not pulling up the original memory—you're remembering the last time you remembered it. The original is already gone.
We call them "white lies" as if the color makes them more forgivable, but they're really just practice lies.
Your skeleton is the most honest thing about you—it's literally what you're built on, and you'll never see it until you're done using it.
People keep asking what you want to be when you grow up, but nobody asks what you want to feel like.
The saddest part of being human is knowing exactly what would make you happy and choosing not to do it anyway.
You can't step in the same river twice, but you can have the same recurring dream three hundred times and never fully understand it.
Mirrors show you what you look like, but they've never shown you how you actually move through the world.
We spend our whole lives collecting experiences we'll probably forget, and the things we do remember don't matter nearly as much as we thought they would.
Time is the only currency that becomes more valuable the less you have left of it.
Your voice sounds different to everyone in the room—physically different, because sound travels differently to each ear. You're literally a different person to each listener.
The scariest realization isn't that we're alone in the universe; it's that we might not be and we'll never know.
You can know how to do something perfectly and still mess it up every time because knowing and doing are two completely different skills.
Every problem you're worried about right now will either be solved or won't matter in five years, but you won't know which until then.
The only applause you'll ever hear is from other people—you'll never know what your own accomplishment sounds like from the outside.
Guilt is proof you have a conscience, but it's also proof that you haven't actually changed anything about the situation yet.

darkjoke.thought:
I told my girlfriend she drew her eyebrows too high.
She looked surprised.
I have a stepladder because my real ladder left when I was just a kid.

My dentist told me I need to floss more.
I said, "Doc, I'm already hanging by a thread."

I'm reading a book on the history of glue.
Can't put it down.

My therapist asked how my childhood was.
I said, "Well, I'm here, aren't I?"

I wanted to make a joke about my dead grandpa.
But he's not here to laugh at it. Mostly because he's dead.

People keep asking if I'm okay.
I tell them yes, then spend the next three hours wondering why they asked.

I joined a gym to get fit.
Turns out they meant physically.

My friend said he was going to kill himself over his credit card debt.
I said, "You could just declare bankruptcy."
He said, "That's not as permanent."

I've been trying to eat healthier.
So far I've just developed an expensive relationship with disappointment.

My wife asked why I never smile in photos.
I said, "Because I know how they end."

I told my boss I was leaving the job to pursue my dreams.
He said, "That's great!"
I said, "No, I mean literally right now, in my car, before you call security."
The worst time to have a heart attack is during a game of charades.

I got fired from my job at the suicide hotline.
Apparently, "just do it" isn't the right approach.

My doctor said I need to cut back on drinking.
I said, "I'm not a patient man."
He said, "Exactly."

I've been diagnosed with short-term memory loss.
I've been diagnosed with short-term memory loss.

My wife said she needs space.
So I locked her in the basement—it's technically more confined, but the concept is there.

I'm starting a support group for people who talk too much.
First meeting is next week. I'll probably spend it alone.

My parents said I was a disappointment.
Now I'm a well-adjusted disappointment with a mortgage.

I asked the pharmacist if antidepressants had side effects.
He said, "Only if you stop taking them."
